attempts.label: OPENNEURO:ds000228
attempts.entry_title: Development of the social brain from age three to twelve (Richardson et al. 2018)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Richardson, Lisandrelli, Riobueno-Naylor and Saxe (2018) on OpenNeuro ds000228, which holds movie-viewing fMRI of 122 children aged 3 to 12 and 33 adults, with the paper's preprocessed images, artifact and CompCor regressors, group ROIs and behavioural scores. It covers the behavioural results, motion, inter-region correlations within and across the ToM and pain networks, reverse correlation of network timecourses, functional maturity, and the face-region analyses.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Richardson et al. (2018) from OpenNeuro ds000228

outcomes.statement: The sample is 122 children aged 3.5 to 12 years (64 female) and 33 adults aged 18 to 39 (20 female); five further children were excluded for excessive motion. By age group there are 17, 14, 34, 23 and 34 children aged 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 to 12 years.

outcomes.quote: One hundred twenty two 3.5–12-year-old children (M(s.d.) = 6.7 (2.3); 64 females) participated in the study
outcomes.notes: All nine counts match exactly and the mean child age is 6.71 years (s.d. 2.33). The age ranges of the five child groups match Supplementary Table 1. The five children excluded for motion are not in the dataset, so that part of the statement cannot be checked beyond the absence of any participant with one third or more artifact timepoints (maximum 48 of 168).

outcomes.statement: In adults, within-ToM (mean z .48) and within-Pain (.35) correlations are strongly positive and the across-network correlation is negative (-.17), each within-network value exceeding the across-network value.
outcomes.source: Results, Inter-region correlation analysis, paragraph 2; Figure 2
outcomes.quote: In adults, each network exhibited strong positive correlations within-network, and strong negative correlations across network

statistics.test: paired sample two-tailed t-test
paired sample two-tailed t-test

outcomes.notes: Main reading (O1 all voxels of the deposited masks, O2a, O3a). Adult means within-ToM .604, within-Pain .398, across -.051; paired t within-ToM against across 19.1 and within-Pain against across 21.8, both p < 1e-18. The two t values are in tolerance under three of the four O2 and O3 readings; the three means are out of tolerance under all. O1 with only voxels with data gives identical values. Variants outside the paper's method (no high-pass, 50 s high-pass, no CompCor) give adult means from .556 to .645 within-ToM and -.051 to .059 across, none near the paper's. Further diagnostic variants, adults (within-ToM, within-Pain, across), are mean r in place of z .519, .354, -.049; the high-pass basis in the nuisance regression .593, .393, -.086; left and right M1 as two regressors .599, .390, -.037; and the mean ToM and Pain signal as an added regressor .286, .258, -.382. Only the last, which is not the paper's method, moves the across value past the paper's, and it also takes both within-network values well below the paper's (.286 and .258 against .48 and .35). A shared signal removed in the paper's processing would shift the across value in this direction, but this variant does not match the paper's pattern, and no step of the Methods accounts for the offset. The ROI masks are in MNI mm (9 mm sphere centroids within 3.7 mm of the stated centers, every voxel within 8.9 mm), and the images are int16 with no scaling. Fig. 2 shows the mean matrices only as colours, so the offset cannot be traced pair by pair; the adult and 3yo mean matrices are printed in the notebook.
deviations: The 100 s high-pass filter is SPM's discrete cosine basis (spm_filter); the Methods say SPM8 and "a cutoff of 100 s" without naming the filter. A standard choice.
The cleaning is applied to the ROI mean timecourse, which equals cleaning each voxel and averaging, as every step of Methods paragraph 4 is linear and the same for each voxel.

outcomes.notes: Williams' T2 (and Steiger's Z, which agrees) on the age correlations of irc-control-networks. Under both readings (partial with motion, or plain Spearman) and every pipeline reading, the six differences the paper finds significant are significant in the same direction (main reading, reading a, t = 2.51 to 5.03 for Face and V1 against ToM and Pain; -2.95 and -4.0 for across ToM-Pain against Face-Scene and M1-V1). outcomes.notes: The best-matching reading is O5a (p < .05 uncorrected); O6 changes nothing for the ToM and Pain networks. It finds 9 ToM events (80 s, mean 8.9 s) and 10 pain events (84 s, mean 8.4 s), covering all 7 ToM events and 10 of 12 pain events of Supplementary Table 3 (P08 and P10 missed). Under O5b and O5c, 7 ToM events (56 s, all 7 table events) and 8 pain events (62 s, 8 of 12). The pain time is in tolerance under O5a, the ToM time under none; the counts never both match. At least 5 of 7 and 9 of 12 table events are found under O5a, the partial outcome. Peak TRs of the found ToM events (131, 95, 64, 150, 46, 125, 54) are within one TR of the table's.

outcomes.statement: ToM and pain events overlap at a single timepoint (the last of T05 and first of P05), less overlap than chance in a permutation test.
outcomes.source: Results, Reverse correlation analysis, paragraph 2; Methods, fMRI data analysis, paragraph 10

statistics.test: random timecourse permutations with the same number and duration of events
statistics.statistic: 5/1000 permutations with at most one timepoint of overlap

outcomes.notes: The found events (O5a) overlap at no timepoint, against 1 in the paper; permutation p = .002 under reading (a), 158 TRs, and p < .001 (0 of 1000) under reading (b), 159 TRs (mean permuted overlap 11.9 TRs under both). Under O5b and O5c the overlap is also 0, p = .019 to .049. With the paper's own events (Supplementary Table 3, variant) the overlap is 1 TR, p = .002 and .008. Less overlap than chance holds; the overlap count does not match. The criterion states only when the claim is reproduced. The outcome is partial because the claim's test (p <= .01) holds and only its expected count is out of tolerance, the case the claims file's Rule S and the protocol call partial; irc-williams is not reproduced because two of the paper's tests fail there. The verifier would give not_reproduced in round 2; the disagreement is recorded under verifications.
deviations: Seed fixed (a standard choice); the random gaps split the remaining zeros by a multinomial draw after one zero between events, a reading of Methods paragraph 10, which says only "a random proportion of zeros between events".

Reading (b) of the criterion is run as 159-TR timecourses (159 minus each network's event TRs as zeros), the length implied by the paper's zeros (125, 116) and event totals (34, 43 TRs); with the Supplementary Table 3 events it gives 125 and 116 zeros.

The dataset's README lists the events that replicated across the two adult samples; they overlap all seven ToM events and the pain events of Supplementary Table 3 except P08, P09 and P11, as the claim states. The Saxe lab web page (https://saxelab.mit.edu/theory-mind-and-pain-matrix-localizer-movie-viewing-experiment) offers the experiment script movloc.zip (version of 29 March 2019) whose mov_localizer.m holds them, but with no DOI or repository commit, so it cannot be pinned as the protocol requires for an outside input.

findings.statement: With the paper's own deposited preprocessed images, artifact and CompCor regressors and ROI masks, and the pipeline of the Methods, the inter-region correlations differ from the paper's, higher within networks and less negative across them (adults .604, .398 and -.051 against .48, .35 and -.17). In the 3-year-olds within-ToM is higher (.326 against .21) but within-Pain is lower (.179 against .23; non-bilateral Pain .146 against .17), so the offset is not the same in every group. Several downstream results (within-ToM difference between false-belief passers and failers, age effects at event peaks, the T04 effect of ToM score) do not come out as reported. Either the deposited data or the described pipeline differs from what produced the paper's numbers.

For the authors, which timepoints entered the inter-region correlations (all 168 TRs, or TRs 11 to 168 as in the reverse correlation), and whether the artifact timepoints were regressed with one indicator each? irc-tom-behavior-age, irc-fb-across and maturity-within change outcome with this choice; this attempt assumed all 168 TRs and one indicator each, as in the deposited regressor files.

For the authors, over which timepoints was each ROI timecourse z-normalized before the reverse correlation, and were child event magnitudes taken from the z-normalized timecourse? rc-3yo-events depends on the first (all 168 TRs assumed) and rc-fb-no-difference on the second (z-normalized assumed). The alpha of the reverse-correlation t-tests is also not stated; p < .05 uncorrected matches Supplementary Table 3 best.
The analysis code is available only on request, and the high-pass filter implementation (SPM discrete cosine assumed) is not stated.

participants.tsv lists 2 seven-year-olds and 21 8-12-year-olds with 3.13 mm voxels and no slice gap, where the Methods say 3 and 20. The voxel-size column name is misspelled ("Voxel slize"), and the no-gap level is stored as an empty value where participants.json defines the level "None".

19 participants (14 aged 8-12, 2 adults, one each 4, 5 and 7 years) have face-ROI voxels without data at some timepoint, where Supplementary Fig. 4 counts 17 with incomplete ventral coverage (12 aged 8-12, 2 adults, one each 3, 4 and 7 years); the minimum of 101 voxels with data agrees with its "at least 100 voxels". The coverage criterion may differ.
The independent sample of 20 adults that defined the ToM and pain ROIs and replicated the events is not deposited anywhere; the ROIs it produced are in the dataset.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (verifier-1, same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The summary cell was not removed by the handover, as it shared a cell with the blocked claims, and the verifier read it after forming most of its outcomes. It queried the archive's file list for the blocked claims and tested the helper functions on synthetic inputs. Of 42 claims it agreed with 39 outcomes and disagreed on irc-williams, rc-child-adult-timecourse and maturity-across.

disagreements.reason: Under both Williams readings, within-Pain vs Scene (p .010) and within-Pain vs M1 (p .004) come out significant where the paper has n.s. That is 8/10 comparisons as in the paper, and the criterion has no partial clause.

ToM 3yo r .212 (p .0076) and Pain 3yo .531 are out of tolerance. The 3yo ToM p misses the paper's "all p < .0005" bound, and Pain 3yo/4yo miss its "p < 1e-13" bound. All are significant at the Bonferroni α .01, so a laxer reading of the criterion would give partial. The notebook checks every bin only against p < .0005.
The across-network effects hold (t -4.5 and -3.6, out of tolerance). The within-Pain effect is significant under every reading (p .005 to .018), which fails the criterion's condition.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (verifier-2, same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. Of 42 claims it agreed with 41 outcomes and disagreed on rc-overlap. It found no misreading in the claims file, so no question was added. It also questioned the README's run time, which now gives the times `tools/entry.py all` reported.

disagreements.reason: Disagrees. The criterion defines only a reproduced outcome ("one overlapping timepoint is found and p <= .01 under a reading"), does not invoke Rule S and has no partial clause. The overlap is 0 against 1 with tolerance 0 (cell 86). By the record's reasoning for irc-williams it is not_reproduced. Partial could only be defended by applying Rule S's partial clause, which this criterion does not name; the record should state that reasoning, or change the outcome. In round 1 the verifier agreed and missed this.

entries.name: openneuro-ds000228-richardson-2018
entries.title: Development of the social brain from age three to twelve (Richardson et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Richardson, Lisandrelli, Riobueno-Naylor and Saxe (2018) on OpenNeuro ds000228, which holds movie-viewing fMRI of 122 children aged 3 to 12 and 33 adults, with the paper's preprocessed images, artifact and CompCor regressors, group ROIs and behavioural scores. It covers the behavioural results, motion, inter-region correlations within and across the ToM and pain networks, reverse correlation of network timecourses, functional maturity, and the face-region analyses.
